KEY MESSAGE 1...

The latest mid level water vapor loop shows a well defined shortwave 
spinning slowly east into the northern Mid-Atlantic. Out ahead of 
this feature there is plenty of lift as southwesterly low level jet 
is in place across Central PA and Central NY. There is deep moisture 
extending up and above the 700mb layer. Strong upper level 
divergence is evident across this same area at 250mb to 300mb. There 
is enough elevated instability for a few lightning strikes in the 
heavier precipitation currently across the western Catskills and 
northern Poconos. Further back to the south and southwest there is 
more instability present, with the latest SPC mesoanalysis showing 
500J/Kg of MLCAPE up to Harrisburg and nearly State College in PA. 
Scattered embedded thunderstorms have already developed in this 
area, and these will continue to slowly track off to the north and 
east; becoming more elevated in nature as they move through NE PA 
and portions of Central NY. It seems with this strong lift and 
divergence in place that periods of rain, showers and occasional 
thunderstorms will continue through daybreak and likely even into 
the mid or late morning hours across NE PA and the NY southern 
tier....before completely exiting before noon today. The official 
forecast takes a blend of radar trends, HRRR, 3km NAM and the NBM 
for hourly PoPs this morning. QPF is a blend of WPC, NBM and latest 
observed trends. There will likely be a few localized stripes of 1-
2, perhaps 2.5 inches of rain by the time the rain ends late this 
morning...although most locations will see under 1 inch of rain by 
noon. There could be isolated areas where ponding of water and 
excessive rainfall occur. Can't rule out some localized flash 
flooding as well; and this potential will be monitored very closely.

After the rain exits and ends later this morning there should be 
some dry time and skies turn partly sunny. It will be warm and humid 
today with highs reaching the mid-70s to low 80s and dew points in 
the upper 60s to low 70s expected. This will allow for increases 
surface based instability later this afternoon, along with 
increasing bulk shear values between 40-50 kts. As the cold front 
presses south a scattered line of storms is expected to 
develop...first across the NW Finger Lakes and Syracuse area...then 
reaching the NY southern tier and eventually NE PA/Catskills by mid 
to late evening. These storms could produce heavy downpours, gusty 
to isolated damaging winds and even hail. SPC maintains the Marginal 
Risk (level 1 of 5) for isolated severe storm potential for just 
about the entire CWA later this afternoon and evening.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

A fairly strong cold front is forecast to push through the area 
early Monday morning. Behind the front much cooler and drier air 
will advect into the forecast area. 850mb temperatures fall to 
around +4C by early Monday afternoon. Gusty NW winds are also 
forecast to develop in the cold air advection regime. Expect 
sustained winds of 8-15 mph with some gusts to 25 mph possible as 
the boundary layer becomes well mixed up to 825mb. Despite skies be 
partly to mostly sunny high temperatures are only forecast to reach 
the low to mid-60s across Central NY...with mid-60s to around 70 in 
NE PA. Monday will be quite chilly with widespread valley fog in the 
forecast. There will be a steep low level inversion developing as 
mid level warm air advections begins overnight and 850mb 
temperatures actually rise back to +8C by sunrise. A 1028mb surface 
high will be directly overhead, helping to keep skies clear and 
winds very light. Expect very cool overnight lows ranging from the 
upper 30s to mid-40s in most locations. A few of the normally colder 
spots could even see mid-30s with patchy frost possible.

Tuesday features ample sunshine and warming temperatures as a strong 
upper level ridge pushes into the area from the Ohio Valley. Daytime 
highs should recover into the upper 60s to low 70s, with a few 
locations up in the mid-70s. Winds turn southerly between 8-15 mph, 
which will help to boost the afternoon temperatures.

An upper level ridge nudges north into the area for Wednesday, which 
will bring warmer weather and perhaps a few isolated showers or 
thunderstorms late in the day. The flow turns more zonal by 
Thursday, which will keep the warm temperatures around but bring the 
potential for more showers and thunderstorms. A broad upper level 
trough develops over the Northeast US by Friday, as the strong upper 
level ridge retrogrades into the arklatex region. This will start a 
cooling trend for our area, with still a chance for lingering 
showers. Next weekend looks to feature near average temperatures 
with some shower chances Saturday, then generally dry weather next 
Sunday. Official forecast stuck very close to the blended ensemble 
guidance for this extended period as exact details remain to be seen.
